source_name: MPO — Přehled příjemců dotací ze státního rozpočtu a evropských fondů
why_relevant: Ministry of Industry and Trade's §5(3) FOI publication of state and EU grant recipients. Demonstrates the CZ FOI-driven publication layer that sits under EU-funded procurement — a fallback route to contract-level detail when TED award notices omit values or suppress supplier names.

source_name: NIPEZ podpora – Registr veřejných zakázek (rules & data structures)
why_relevant: Documents the Registr veřejných zakázek: the central record that ingests contract data from all certified electronic tools (not just NEN) and redistributes it to consumers, per MMR-issued data-structure descriptions. Essential for designing collection: it defines the schema and the machine-readable path to the full national corpus including private e-tools.

source_name: Tender arena – seznam profilů zadavatelů (directory)
why_relevant: Directory listing all buyer profiles hosted on Tender arena, including Prague, its městské části (e.g. Praha 3, Praha 10), city companies (THMP, DPP). Efficient way to enumerate one large slice of the decentralised landscape.

entity_name: Výroční zpráva o stavu veřejných zakázek v ČR
source_name: Portál o veřejných zakázkách (portal-vz.cz) – MMR methodology hub
why_relevant: Ministry for Regional Development's authoritative map of the NIPEZ ecosystem: which subsystem publishes what, the uveřejňovací subsystém, IS VZ, NIPEZ commodity catalogue, methodologies, decision databases and annual reports on the state of public procurement. Best single starting node for snowballing further CZ procurement sources and for understanding what is legally required to be published where.

entity_name: Výroční zpráva o stavu veřejných zakázek v ČR
source_name: Portál o veřejných zakázkách – Individuální elektronické nástroje (certified e-tendering tool register)
why_relevant: Official MMR-maintained list of all certified individual electronic tools (elektronické nástroje) usable for e-tendering in CZ, with operator names and tool URLs. This is the master index that enumerates every commercial platform in this cell in one page — E-ZAK/X-EN (QCM), Tenderarena (Tendersystems), Josephine (NAR Marketing/Sentinet), PROEBIZ profily, zadavatel.cz/e-zakazky (OTIDEA), CENT (Osigeno), KDV, eCentre, FirstBuySale (ANETE), x:tendr (RTS), Eveza (NWT), Athena/nasprofil (GC Logix), eZakazky (YOUR SYSTEM), PARC (PXE), plus special-purpose tools.

source_name: RBI — Our network (group entity map)
why_relevant: Authoritative list of RBI's CEE subsidiaries and country presence (Vienna HQ, ~24 countries, 14 key markets). Needed to resolve which legal entity is contracting in a CEE-wide award and to confirm the Czech entity is in scope of a group category strategy.

source_name: Sdružení pro bankovní karty (SBK) – členové / členské banky
why_relevant: The Czech card-payments body: ~18 regular members (financial institutions only) plus ~23 observers, and its statistics pages enumerate contributing issuers/acquirers including non-banks (EVO Payments, Euronet, CCS, Twisto, Essox). For POS/card-terminal procurement this is the precise buyer list. Note two domains in circulation: bankovnikarty.cz (institutional) and bankovni-karty.cz (content).

source_name: Česká bankovní asociace (ČBA) – Členové (member banks directory)
why_relevant: Authoritative roster of ~34 banks and building societies covering >99% of the CZ banking sector. This is the canonical buyer-universe list for A2 tender monitoring: every entity here is a potential contracting entity (some are also sectoral/state-linked buyers) and the list lets us seed profile/entity resolution against tender portals. Note www.cbaonline.cz/o-nas/clenove also appears in search indexes as an alternative path.

source_name: Asseco Central Europe – Reference (CZ) page
why_relevant: Vendor-maintained customer list naming Czech banks and building societies (Česká spořitelna, ČSOB, MONETA, ČSOB stavební spořitelna, Modrá pyramida per search summary). A logo/reference page is the cheapest longitudinal signal of who won which core-banking / building-society estate.

source_name: HlidacStatu/API GitHub repository (apiary.apib spec)
why_relevant: Source-of-truth API blueprint and issue history for the Hlidac endpoints; also reveals the data model (contract fields, party identifiers, classification) that we would mirror in our own store.

source_name: ICT UNIE – Členové ICTU (ICT supplier directory)
why_relevant: 51 regular + 9 honorary members, listed A–Ž with hyperlinks to each company site — the core roster of ICT integrators bidding on Czech public and banking IT tenders (Asseco CE, Atos, AutoCont, České Radiokomunikace, Dell, IBM, Huawei…). Directly answers 'who are the likely bidders/competitors on a given award notice'. English mirror at /en/ictu-members.

source_name: Erste Group Procurement organisational profile on LinkedIn (Procurement Services Ges.m.b.H. / s Proserv)
why_relevant: People-layer pointer: names country managing directors and sourcing specialists per market (including Romania and, by structure, the Czech entity), plus job postings that reveal category coverage and tooling. The email domain erstegroupprocurement.com identified through profile aggregators indicates a separate procurement web presence worth probing directly.

source_name: najdivz.cz and etendry.cz – buyer-profile lookup aggregators
why_relevant: Secondary directories mapping buyer name to profile; useful redundancy against VVZ when a profile URL has moved, and helpful for resolving municipal company names to ICO.

source_name: NajdiVZ – CPV code browser (CZ)
why_relevant: Czech-language browser of the CPV taxonomy including the financial-and-insurance-services division. Practical utility: it gives the exact Czech labels for the CPV codes to filter on (bankovnictví 66110000, zpracování finančních transakcí a služby zúčtovacího střediska 66172000), which is what makes precise CZ-language querying of VVZ/NEN possible.

source_name: SP ČR – Abecední seznam členů (alphabetical member base)
why_relevant: Largest CZ employers' federation; the alphabetical roster mixes large corporates and sector unions, so it broadens the supplier/buyer map beyond finance-only associations (IT integrators, telco, security printing). Companion 'jmenný seznam kontaktů' gives named representatives useful for actor mapping.

source_name: zIndex — wiki metodiky hodnocení zadavatelů (wiki.zindex.cz)
why_relevant: Academic scoring methodology for Czech contracting authorities built on VVZ data, contracting-authority profiles and other tender sources over rolling three-year windows. Its wiki pages document exactly which data fields exist, where they are unreliable, and how supplier dependence (share of public contracts in total revenue) can be computed — a free methodological map of the CZ procurement data landscape and its quality traps.

source_name: Česká fintech asociace (Czech Fintech Association) – Členové
why_relevant: 80+ members/affiliates spanning payment gateways (GoPay, ComGate), card/POS tech (Aevi, MONET+, Wultra), data (CRIF, Dateio) and consultancies (Deloitte). This is the highest-yield map of the CZ payments supplier long tail — i.e. our competitor and partner universe when reading award notices. Bilingual site (cs/en).

source_name: AKAT ČR – Členové asociace (capital market)
why_relevant: Investment companies, foreign fund managers and service providers active in CZ collective investment. Extends the financial-buyer universe beyond banks/leasing into asset management, which procures custody, reporting and payments infrastructure. A historical merged-member list is also archived on the site.

source_name: AMSP ČR – Členská základna (SMEs and collective members)
why_relevant: Membership base is largely collective (guilds, cechy, clusters, professional associations) — which makes it a snowball engine for discovering further niche associations rather than a company list. Relevant for finding SME-side suppliers and the retail-merchant lobby that shapes POS/payments policy.

source_name: APEK – Asociace pro elektronickou komerci, Seznam členů
why_relevant: ~580 e-commerce companies, software vendors and financial institutions. For payments this is the merchant-side demand map (who buys payment gateways, POS, BNPL) plus the certified-shop directory at certifikovany-obchod.cz. A member-only zone exists, so part of the directory may be gated.

source_name: Asociace pro veřejné zakázky (AVZ) – Členové AVZ
why_relevant: The single most on-topic association for workstream A2: AVZ segments its members into zadavatelé (contracting authorities), dodavatelé (suppliers), administrátoři/poradci and advokátní kanceláře. That segmentation is effectively a ready-made buyer/supplier/intermediary map for Czech public procurement, including municipalities that run tenders.

source_name: ATMIA showrooms – vendor profiles (NCR Atleos, Auriga)
why_relevant: Industry-association vendor showroom pages carry vendor-supplied capability and customer claims, and the ATMIA membership roster itself is an actor-map source for who is active in CEE self-service.

source_name: Blue Events – conference calendar (Prague, cross-sector)
why_relevant: Organiser behind Retail Summit and related CZ/SK B2B conferences; its calendar is a pointer to which industry events exist each year and therefore where bank/retail/payment roadmaps get presented.

source_name: Hospodářská komora ČR (komora.cz) – členská základna / oborová sdružení
why_relevant: ~17,000 members organised in 57 territorial chambers and ~140 industry associations. The value is the association index (a master pointer to further sector bodies) and the regional chambers' own member catalogues; a single national supplier catalogue was not located from the surface web, so this is a hub-of-hubs rather than one list.

source_name: Monet+ a.s. – company profile on Czech Digital Solutions catalogue
why_relevant: State-backed export/vendor catalogue profile of Monet+ (digital identity and electronic payment transactions for banks). Such catalogues carry vendor self-descriptions and sometimes reference customers, and the catalogue as a whole is an actor-map source for CZ fintech/payment vendors.

source_name: Open Contracting Partnership Data Registry — Europe / TED (OpenTender) publication record
why_relevant: Registry entry documenting how TED data is republished in OCDS, its coverage and known quality caveats. Good for deciding whether to consume TED directly or via an OCDS mirror, and for finding further CZ-specific OCDS publishers.

source_name: podo.fen.cz – virtuální profily zadavatelů
why_relevant: Third-party service constructing 'virtual buyer profiles' that consolidate a buyer's tenders across platforms — useful as a cross-check when a municipality has migrated between e-tools and older notices are stranded.

source_name: SPIR – Sdružení pro internetový rozvoj, Členové
why_relevant: Internet-economy roster including banks as members (ČSOB observed), media, adtech and technology vendors (Adform, SAS Institute ČR, Seznam.cz, RTB House). Weaker for tenders than ICT UNIE/AVZ but useful for mapping digital-marketing and data suppliers that banks procure from. Legacy English member list exists at old.spir.cz.

entity_name: Svaz měst a obcí ČR + regional unions
source_name: Svaz měst a obcí ČR + regional unions (SMO ČR / SMOJK) – member municipality lists
why_relevant: Municipalities are the highest-volume contracting authorities in CZ public procurement, including for cash handling, POS/e-payment for local fees and IT. Regional unions publish itemised member lists (SMOJK: 131 members as of Aug 2025); the national SMO ČR site did not surface an open itemised roster, so regional unions plus the RÚIAN/ARES obce registries are the practical route.

source_name: Transparency International Česká republika – kauzy
why_relevant: Anti-corruption NGO documenting procurement cases and the functioning of ÚOHS itself (the regulator that rules on contested tenders). Media cite it heavily; its case pages point to the underlying tenders and actors.

source_name: Verifone – partner taxonomy page for Printec Czech Republic, s.r.o.
why_relevant: Vendor partner/distributor directories reveal the supply chain behind CZ POS estates: who is authorised to deploy which terminal brand. Printec CZ appearing as a Verifone partner is an indirect indicator of which acquirer estates it can serve.

source_name: Česká asociace pojišťoven (ČAP) – Řádní členové
why_relevant: 25 insurers covering >98% of the CZ insurance market. Insurers are adjacent financial buyers of the same core-systems, payments and document-output vendors as banks, and several are bancassurance arms of ČBA members — useful for group-level buyer resolution. Archive mirror at archiv.cap.cz preserves older rosters; English section exists.

source_name: ČLFA – Seznam členských společností (leasing & consumer finance members)
why_relevant: ~35 leasing/consumer-finance companies (Ayvens, Arval, Bibby, captive OEM finance arms). These are non-bank financial buyers of POS/payment/IT services that keyword tender searches rarely surface; each member has its own detail page on clfa.cz, giving structured company records.
